summary: Barry Divola reviews two December 2023 albums in The Age: Tate McRae's Think Later, her second album after the viral hit Greedy, and Peter Gabriel's I/O, his first new original solo material in over two decades. He finds McRae's album uneven, with Tedder-produced ballads dragging down the Y2K-flavoured best tracks, and Gabriel's album thoughtful about mortality but overlong and overcooked.
one_line: Barry Divola reviews Tate McRae's viral-hit follow-up Think Later and Peter Gabriel's long-awaited, overlong comeback album I/O.
key_facts: Tate McRae is 20 years old, was born in Calgary, and has been a professionally trained dancer since age 6.
At 13 Tate McRae finished third on the US version of So You Think You Can Dance and drew record label attention with songs uploaded to YouTube.
McRae's 2020 song You Broke Me First had a chart moment, leading to her 2022 debut album I Used To Think I Can Fly, which had production from Greg Kurstin and Finneas.
Greedy went viral in August 2023 after use by TikToker Tube Girl and in hair-flip transition clips, amassing over 320 million streams globally and topping charts internationally.
Greedy earned McRae a slot on Saturday Night Live and sold-out shows for her Australian tour next November.
McRae's Think Later is almost completely produced and co-written with Ryan Tedder of OneRepublic; the reviewer finds his midtempo ballads such as Cut My Hair, Grave and Stay Done slick but dour.

The best Think Later tracks per the review are Exes, Hurt My Feelings and Guilty Conscience, which follow the Greedy template of Timbaland-style Y2K beats; We're Not Alike is a post-punky track built on an Interpol-ish riff.
Peter Gabriel's I/O is his first solo album of new original material in over two decades; the review calls it overcooked and overlong, and notes some wags call it his Chinese Democracy.
Gabriel is 73, and I/O is marked by a sense of mortality; And Still was written to deal with the death of his mother in 2016.
Gabriel's Sledgehammer (1986) was the most played video on MTV, and In Your Eyes featured in the 1989 film Say Anything.
I/O opens with Panopticom, which features Gabriel's gated drum sound and the bass of long-time bassist Tony Levin.
I/O comes in two mixes: a 'bright-side mix' by Mark 'Spike' Stent and a 'dark-side mix' by Tchad Blake.
Gabriel's Live and Let Live was inspired by Nelson Mandela and The Elders project but criticised as full of cliches.
